newsitem.title: USA: IMF confident on Argentina with or without program.
newsitem.headline: IMF confident on Argentina with or without program.

text.p: International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said Thursday that he had confidence in Argentina's prospects whether it renewed its current IMF program or not.

Camdessus told a news conference that he had not yet talked to Argentine authorities to see whether they would seek to turn a standby agreement that expires in January into a longer-term extended fund facility.
"With or without a program, after Argentina's magnificent efforts during the past years, I am very confident in the future of that country," he said.

Argentina's Economy Minister, Roque Fernandez, was quoted this month in a Buenos Aires newspaper interview as saying that he may settle for another standby agreement rather than for a longer-term program with the IMF.
Fernandez argued that it would be difficult for the government to commit itself to deadlines to approve measures like labor reforms, which require congressional action.
Camdessus, speaking in Spanish, said he had not heard yet about Argentina's intentions but hoped to take a closer look at the issue when he visits Buenos Aires in May.
The IMF thinks that Argentina's current program is achieving good results, despite the recession it suffered in 1995 in the wake of the Mexican peso crisis, he said.

"Now inflation is very close to zero, (GDP) growth was of about 4.5 percent in 1996 and will continue well in that direction during 1997, I think, and our program's goals for end-1996 were met," he said.

The IMF could now help Argentina in several ways, Camdessus said, by either agreeing on a formal program, or a staff monitor program, or by simply continuing their dialogue with the government on deciding policies.
"I don't know what the government's choice will be. I don't know if the measures that they may include in a program would be sufficient or not for our board to okay that program," he said.
